They used Bun 1.4.2 with `--no-env-file --conditions=source --eval`, actual source Layers and installed FetchHttpClient, substituted `FetchHttpClient.Fetch`, synthetic configuration and native Response objects. Both the original probe and a scoped-client control exited 0. No suite, build, negative fixture, credential, provider or state operation was run.
+
+## F1 — P2: explicitly scope native HTTP attempts before early response rejection
+
+Locations at target:
+
+- `packages/analytics/src/live.layer.ts:111-116`: returns rejected before reading response.stream; actual client captured at line 41 and executed at lines 93-110.
+- `apps/web/src/lib/analytics/relay/relay.adapter.layer.ts:199-203`: returns redirect before reading response.stream; actual client captured at line 58 and executed at lines 181-198.
+- `packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/management.adapter.layer.ts:118-122`: filterStatus rejects 3xx before the bounded response collection begins.
+
+Consequence: a rejected or redirected reply with an unfinished body leaves its native fetch request open when the operation's Effect scope has closed. It can retain network/body resources until garbage collection. The operation's advertised five-second lifetime does not determine cleanup for this early branch. Collection is currently off, so this is a candidate activation/lifecycle defect, not observed Production event loss or tax-data disclosure.
+
+Mechanism and direct evidence: installed `node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpClient.ts:864-895` creates a normal AbortController unless the request has been scoped with HttpClient.withScope. An unread normal response is registered in the FinalizationRegistry (`2214-2240`). Reading response.stream aborts through its finaliser (`2317-2325`), but these early branches never read it. Merely enclosing the program in Effect.scoped does not register that AbortController with its Scope. The installed withScope operation explicitly adds that finaliser (`2053-2065`).
+
+Actual original probe, at return from each operation:
+
+| Operation/reply | Result | Native signal aborted | Body used |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Backend 302 | rejected | false | false |
+| Backend 500 | rejected | false | false |
+| Relay 302 | redirect | false | false |
+| Management read 302 | provider-failure | false | false |
+| Backend 200, closed body | accepted | true | true |
+| Relay 429, closed body | 429 | true | true |
+
+Smallest correction: apply installed HttpClient.withScope to the actual client/attempt, inside the already owned per-operation scope, before status filtering or other early response handling. Keep the same safe error, one-attempt, redirect and byte policies. In the control probe, supplying that client changed all four false abort results to true without consuming the rejected bodies or changing results. No source correction was made by this reviewer.
+
+Required focused proof: use the real FetchHttpClient with substituted Fetch that captures RequestInit.signal and returns a native 302/500 Response with a never-ending body. Assert the existing safe result, exactly one request, and signal.aborted immediately after the operation exits. Cover backend rejection, relay redirect, management redirect, success, deadline and interruption. Do not rely on an artificial fixture Scope finaliser as the oracle for native fetch cleanup. The current relay fixture adds its own finaliser at relay.boundary.test.ts:100-109; it proves that finaliser ran, not that Fetch's controller was registered.
+
+Impact owner: analytics backend live Layer, Website relay adapter, PostHog management adapter and their native-transport focused tests. Change required for affected qualification receipts and any acceptance claim; preserve collection-off, sender/project choices, tax results and provider state. This deterministic native signal finding is separate from the previously declared Miniflare/Node bridge's inability to expose actual upstream cancellation. It does not claim live Cloudflare socket termination or final hosted carrier headers.
+
+## F2 — P3: native bodyless success is reported as a backend transport error
+
+Location: `packages/analytics/src/live.layer.ts:117-124`. A successful 204 passes the status check but every stream error becomes AnalyticsCaptureError(reason=transport).
+
+Consequence: an ordinary bodyless successful response is falsely reported as dropped. It has no tax-response or privacy effect and does not reverse a provider-accepted event. Its smaller significance is the wrong disposition/diagnostic and a status test that gives false confidence about the real native transport.
+
+Direct evidence: installed `node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpClientResponse.ts:351-372` returns typed EmptyBodyError for a native Response with no body. The approved actual-Layer probe returning `new Response(null, { status: 204 })` produced backend `transport`, not `accepted`. Native relay 204 succeeded because it handles only this named empty-body case. Backend test `packages/analytics/test/service.test.ts:155-193` expects 204 accepted but uses HttpServerResponse.toClientResponse with an empty stream (`165-173`), which bypasses native fromWeb's null-body behaviour.
+
+Smallest correction: treat only the native typed EmptyBodyError as an empty successful reply after the existing 2xx check. Continue to map all other stream failures to the current safe transport error. Extend the existing 204 case with actual FetchHttpClient/Response(null) coverage; retain 200/299, rejected statuses, failed stream, oversize, deadline and interruption assertions. No new retry or special provider status policy is needed.
+
+Impact owner: private analytics backend Layer and its status/response test. Change required for its direct proof and affected receipt. Preserve app response behaviour, capture payload and provider proof limits.
+
+## Requirements reviewed without another material finding
+
+- Fixed minimal backend encoding accepts catalogue identity/name and required operational/event labels; no calculation input, result, visitor, URL or caller header enters its payload. Explicit deny/off makes no request or UUID. Invalid enabled configuration stays a named failure.
+- One API decorator records successful calculations; metadata and failed work do not register. The request accumulator is bounded at 64, with independent policy/Ref per call. HTTP, RPC and both MCP composition paths use this owner; registration omits the first caller's collector. Native waitUntil preserves call context while each send opens its own operation scope. Pure tax/local SDK paths remain separate.
+- Relay checks fixed path/US destination, exact origin, method, closed retry query and media types; retains complete bytes and uses failing stream bounds. Denied policy precedes body read/delivery. Status/retry projection and caller-header rebuilding are narrow. Streamed success, size crossing and timeout paths are distinct from F1's unconsumed rejection branch.
+- Management inventories complete checked pages and every listed project, rejects incomplete/foreign/ambiguous ownership, bounds reads, serialises writes, and does not automatically repeat an uncertain POST. Provider read/diff/reconcile refuse missing retained history or owner replacement. Ordinary delete and bulk nuke retention are explicit. Live registration caches fallible management acquisition without a package/runtime escape.
+
+## Limits, recovery and return to owner
+
+This review does not choose or implement a browser sender, one-project target, cross-app adoption, credential policy, analytics activation, telemetry/metrics, deployment, provider apply, package publication or merge. The two-project graph was un-applied at the reviewed target; the parent's later single-project revision needs its own matching review/proof. The sender and stored-event/final hosted-header requirements remain unfinished, not new findings here. Retained tax results are unchanged.

# TaxKit repository guide

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Operating loop

1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
   never reopen completed work as policy.
4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
   non-claims, and rollback.

For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the repository-local
`$docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.

## Engineering guardrails

- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at

# TaxKit repository guide

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Operating loop

1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
   never reopen completed work as policy.
4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
   non-claims, and rollback.

For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the repository-local
`$docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.

## Task routes

- Repository and package topology:
  [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md), then
  [`docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md).
- Effect services and boundaries:
  [`docs/architecture/effect-services.md`](docs/architecture/effect-services.md)
  and the applicable package README.
- API/SDK: [`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`](docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md),
  [`apps/api/README.md`](apps/api/README.md), and
  [`packages/sdk/typescript/README.md`](packages/sdk/typescript/README.md).
- Calculators/rules/facts: the focused owner under `docs/architecture/` and the
  owning package README.
- Frontend/public docs:
  [`docs/architecture/frontend.md`](docs/architecture/frontend.md),
  [`docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md`](docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md),
  and [`apps/web/README.md`](apps/web/README.md). The retained old app
  belongs to the existing [docs deployment procedure](docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md).
- Current work: [`docs/product-specs/index.md`](docs/product-specs/index.md) and
  [`docs/exec-plans/active/README.md`](docs/exec-plans/active/README.md).
- Standards, tests, and release checks:
  [`docs/standards/README.md`](docs/standards/README.md) and
  [`docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md`](docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md).
- Repeatable release, versioning, packed-consumer and recovery operations:
  [`docs/runbooks/README.md`](docs/runbooks/README.md) and
  [`docs/operations/authority-model.md`](docs/operations/authority-model.md).
- References and audits: [`docs/references/README.md`](docs/references/README.md)
  and [`docs/documentation-audit/README.md`](docs/documentation-audit/README.md).

Use the repository-owned [Linear skill](.agents/skills/linear/SKILL.md) when
work is tracked in Linear. The [strict Effect skill](.agents/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md)
and [Alchemy skill](.agents/skills/alchemy-iac/SKILL.md) supply methods; local
profiles and the installed dependency graph own TaxKit compatibility. Skill
installation does not imply that the clean-slate enforcement migration is complete.

## Engineering guardrails

- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at
  explicit boundaries.
- Reuse owning Schemas and schema-derived types. Do not mirror raw `id: string`,
  DTOs, provider types, primitive semantic config, or unchecked SDK output.
- Keep primary Effects flat, sequential, and pipe-first where that clarifies
  data flow. Keep one-use mapping/decoding/error logic inline; reject
  helper/common/utils sprawl and generic SDK callback wrappers.
- Keep service contracts, live Layers, test Layers, and executable composition
  separate. Do not run Effects or build live Layers inside domain logic.
- Provider clients expose named Effect operations, `Config.schema` with
  redacted secrets, immediate Schema decoding, safe tagged errors without
  `instanceof`, and live/mock Layers.
- React composition flows route → policy-owning container → focused leaf.
  Routes own transport restoration/outcome matching, containers own commands
  and coordination, and leaves render readonly values/local interaction state.
- Admit an abstraction only with semantic weight, an owner, a real reuse or
  substitution point, a simpler call graph, and focused proof.

## Authority and proof

Tool access is capability, not authority. Provider, registry, publication,
release, deployment, credential, and destructive operations require a named
principal, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary, receipt,
rollback/revocation, and readback. Local gates do not prove publication,
production, or external consumer behavior.

Use `bun run check:repository-paths` for checkout portability and
`bun run verification` for repository closeout. Use `bun run release:check`
only for its documented local release-evidence graph; it does not authorize or
prove publication.

# `@taxkit/analytics`

Private compiled contracts for the accepted page visit and successful hosted
calculator events. The current backend Layer sends only the catalogue ID and
name, fixed application/stage labels, an event UUID and timestamp. It never
accepts tax inputs, results, browser identity, request URLs or request headers.
Tax rule packages and local SDK calculations do not depend on this package.

## Exports

- `./schemas`: public Schemas, brands, and derived types.
- `./errors`: public typed failures.
- `./config`: checked collection mode and capture settings. Off needs no token;
  invalid enabled settings fail with `AnalyticsConfigurationError`.
- `./collection-policy`: one checked incoming-header policy used by the API and Website. Missing allows direct clients; malformed or denied flags and `DNT: 1` refuse collection.
- `./service`: public Effect service contract.
- `./live`: production Layer; compose only at an application/runtime boundary.
- `./test`: deterministic contract-level test Layer.
- `./testing/fixtures`: narrow test fixtures.
- `./testing/observations`: narrow test observation types.

The application supplies native `FetchHttpClient` and Effect `Crypto`. Each
backend send owns one scope and one five-second limit covering identity,
encoding, headers and the complete reply. Replies are limited to 64 KiB. A
request has one attempt, omits credentials, disables trace propagation and
refuses redirects. Disabled or denied collection makes no request and generates
no UUID. `accepted` means a successful HTTP response; stored provider events
require separate readback.

The browser contract is shared so the Website adapter can keep its SDK private.
That adapter and the Website relay remain T008 work in progress. The
[API application owner](../../apps/api/README.md#analytics-candidate) adds the
single successful-use operation; its actual native transport checks remain
separate from this package's tests. A test Layer is substitution proof, not SDK
or browser privacy proof.

## Documentation impact

Change required: this README, the repository
[package ownership](../../docs/architecture/package-ownership.md),
[Effect boundary owner](../../docs/architecture/effect-services.md) and
[active plan](../../docs/exec-plans/active/clean-slate-foundation.md) route these
contracts and pending application work. Preserve: tax Schemas, results, HTTP
and SDK contracts, public accepted documentation and the five existing runbook
procedures. This package is private and is not part of the published tax/SDK
closure, so its addition alone needs no Changeset.

## Runbook applicability

The [deployment runbook](../../docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md) and
[recovery runbook](../../docs/runbooks/recovery.md) own later analytics resource
plans, authority, retained projects, recovery and readback. Tests use controlled
transports and synthetic capture tokens; they perform no provider operation.
Local and ordinary Preview collection must stay off. Production or a controlled
Preview requires checked settings and separately qualified app composition.

## Non-claims

These package checks do not prove the real browser SDK, app composition,
provider project ownership, ingestion, deployment, release publication or
exactly-once storage. Shared Axiom metrics remain deferred by Cooper.

# `@taxkit/analytics`

Private compiled contracts for the accepted page visit and successful hosted
calculator events. The current backend Layer sends only the catalogue ID and
name, fixed application/stage labels, an event UUID and timestamp. It never
accepts tax inputs, results, browser identity, request URLs or request headers.
Tax rule packages and local SDK calculations do not depend on this package.

## Exports

- `./schemas`: public Schemas, brands, and derived types.
- `./errors`: public typed failures.
- `./config`: checked collection mode and capture settings. Off needs no token;
  invalid enabled settings fail with `AnalyticsConfigurationError`.
- `./collection-policy`: one checked incoming-header policy used by the API and Website. Missing allows direct clients; malformed or denied flags and `DNT: 1` refuse collection.
- `./service`: public Effect service contract.
- `./live`: production Layer; compose only at an application/runtime boundary.
- `./test`: deterministic contract-level test Layer.
- `./testing/fixtures`: narrow test fixtures.
- `./testing/observations`: narrow test observation types.

The application supplies native `FetchHttpClient` and Effect `Crypto`. Each
backend send owns one scope and one five-second limit covering identity,
encoding, headers and the complete reply. Replies are limited to 64 KiB. A
request has one attempt, omits credentials, disables trace propagation and
refuses redirects. Disabled or denied collection makes no request and generates
no UUID. `accepted` means a successful HTTP response; stored provider events
require separate readback.

The browser contract is shared so the Website adapter can keep its SDK private.
That adapter and the Website relay remain T008 work in progress. The
[API application owner](../../apps/api/README.md#analytics-candidate) adds the
single successful-use operation; its actual native transport checks remain
separate from this package's tests. A test Layer is substitution proof, not SDK
or browser privacy proof.

Target: `cc11c6aa04665b4014d14953cd2c1379373b2ef7` in `crcorbett/taxkit`.
Observed: 2026-10-07 23:52:32 UTC.
Scope: implemented T008 backend, Website relay and retained-project management.

Authority: bounded read-only delegated review. Only this private report is written.
Outcome: one material cleanup finding and one smaller response-classification finding. This report does not accept T008, T010 or the rebuild.

## Snapshot and method

The checkout was clean at the target commit at entry. Source, tasks and dated records were read using `git show` at that commit. Immediately before the probes, `git diff --exit-code` confirmed all imported analytics, relay and PostHog source paths still matched that target. Parent changes to the un-applied project graph are outside this review.

Read AGENTS.md, docs/README.md, the SPEC Product analytics section, CSF-T008 and CSF-T010 tasks, owning analytics/infrastructure/API/Website READMEs, Effect architecture, and repository-local prd-implementer, docs-maintainer/profile, strict-effect-ts and Alchemy instructions/references. The docs impact mode is report-only candidate.

Reviewed implementation:

- All source under `packages/analytics/src/`, its export map and schema/service tests.
- All source under `packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/`, `alchemy.posthog.run.ts`, management boundary tests and native project-plan tests.
- `apps/api/src/analytics-request.boundary.ts`, `calculator-analytics.layer.ts`, and their real composition/call sites in `worker.ts`, `worker.application.ts` and `mcp-session.layer.ts`; request boundary tests.
- All Website relay source, its boundary tests, native relay/analytics tests, server routing and runtime composition.
- Backend/request, Website-policy, retained-project and relay qualified receipts. Every addressable raw log digest referenced by those four records matched its receipt. Digest agreement is custody evidence, not a new run or proof that each assertion covers every requirement.

Installed source owns compatibility: Effect 4.0.0, Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80, Distilled PostHog 1.0.0-rc.13, platform-node 4.0.0. Inspected actual FetchHttpClient, HttpClient, HttpClientResponse, byte-limit stream, native Worker/DO waitUntil and Alchemy plan adoption behaviour. The available Effect reference at `92f48401426694eb1d9d0552b2f7514b3978e7f4` uses the older separate platform layout; the Alchemy reference at `808ef694b2e742a2bb76cb301da371e71421fa57` is beta.75. Neither selects the receiving APIs or an upgrade.

The parent expressly authorised memory-only native Fetch probes, without network or source writes. They used Bun 1.4.2 with `--no-env-file --conditions=source --eval`, actual source Layers and installed FetchHttpClient, substituted `FetchHttpClient.Fetch`, synthetic configuration and native Response objects. Both the original probe and a scoped-client control exited 0. No suite, build, negative fixture, credential, provider or state operation was run.

## F1 — P2: explicitly scope native HTTP attempts before early response rejection

Locations at target:

- `packages/analytics/src/live.layer.ts:111-116`: returns rejected before reading response.stream; actual client captured at line 41 and executed at lines 93-110.
- `apps/web/src/lib/analytics/relay/relay.adapter.layer.ts:199-203`: returns redirect before reading response.stream; actual client captured at line 58 and executed at lines 181-198.
- `packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/management.adapter.layer.ts:118-122`: filterStatus rejects 3xx before the bounded response collection begins.

Consequence: a rejected or redirected reply with an unfinished body leaves its native fetch request open when the operation's Effect scope has closed. It can retain network/body resources until garbage collection. The operation's advertised five-second lifetime does not determine cleanup for this early branch. Collection is currently off, so this is a candidate activation/lifecycle defect, not observed Production event loss or tax-data disclosure.

Mechanism and direct evidence: installed `node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpClient.ts:864-895` creates a normal AbortController unless the request has been scoped with HttpClient.withScope. An unread normal response is registered in the FinalizationRegistry (`2214-2240`). Reading response.stream aborts through its finaliser (`2317-2325`), but these early branches never read it. Merely enclosing the program in Effect.scoped does not register that AbortController with its Scope. The installed withScope operation explicitly adds that finaliser (`2053-2065`).

Actual original probe, at return from each operation:

| Operation/reply | Result | Native signal aborted | Body used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Backend 302 | rejected | false | false |
| Backend 500 | rejected | false | false |
| Relay 302 | redirect | false | false |
| Management read 302 | provider-failure | false | false |
| Backend 200, closed body | accepted | true | true |
| Relay 429, closed body | 429 | true | true |

Smallest correction: apply installed HttpClient.withScope to the actual client/attempt, inside the already owned per-operation scope, before status filtering or other early response handling. Keep the same safe error, one-attempt, redirect and byte policies. In the control probe, supplying that client changed all four false abort results to true without consuming the rejected bodies or changing results. No source correction was made by this reviewer.

Required focused proof: use the real FetchHttpClient with substituted Fetch that captures RequestInit.signal and returns a native 302/500 Response with a never-ending body. Assert the existing safe result, exactly one request, and signal.aborted immediately after the operation exits. Cover backend rejection, relay redirect, management redirect, success, deadline and interruption. Do not rely on an artificial fixture Scope finaliser as the oracle for native fetch cleanup. The current relay fixture adds its own finaliser at relay.boundary.test.ts:100-109; it proves that finaliser ran, not that Fetch's controller was registered.

Impact owner: analytics backend live Layer, Website relay adapter, PostHog management adapter and their native-transport focused tests. Change required for affected qualification receipts and any acceptance claim; preserve collection-off, sender/project choices, tax results and provider state. This deterministic native signal finding is separate from the previously declared Miniflare/Node bridge's inability to expose actual upstream cancellation. It does not claim live Cloudflare socket termination or final hosted carrier headers.

## F2 — P3: native bodyless success is reported as a backend transport error

Location: `packages/analytics/src/live.layer.ts:117-124`. A successful 204 passes the status check but every stream error becomes AnalyticsCaptureError(reason=transport).

Consequence: an ordinary bodyless successful response is falsely reported as dropped. It has no tax-response or privacy effect and does not reverse a provider-accepted event. Its smaller significance is the wrong disposition/diagnostic and a status test that gives false confidence about the real native transport.

Direct evidence: installed `node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpClientResponse.ts:351-372` returns typed EmptyBodyError for a native Response with no body. The approved actual-Layer probe returning `new Response(null, { status: 204 })` produced backend `transport`, not `accepted`. Native relay 204 succeeded because it handles only this named empty-body case. Backend test `packages/analytics/test/service.test.ts:155-193` expects 204 accepted but uses HttpServerResponse.toClientResponse with an empty stream (`165-173`), which bypasses native fromWeb's null-body behaviour.

Smallest correction: treat only the native typed EmptyBodyError as an empty successful reply after the existing 2xx check. Continue to map all other stream failures to the current safe transport error. Extend the existing 204 case with actual FetchHttpClient/Response(null) coverage; retain 200/299, rejected statuses, failed stream, oversize, deadline and interruption assertions. No new retry or special provider status policy is needed.

Impact owner: private analytics backend Layer and its status/response test. Change required for its direct proof and affected receipt. Preserve app response behaviour, capture payload and provider proof limits.

## Requirements reviewed without another material finding

- Fixed minimal backend encoding accepts catalogue identity/name and required operational/event labels; no calculation input, result, visitor, URL or caller header enters its payload. Explicit deny/off makes no request or UUID. Invalid enabled configuration stays a named failure.
- One API decorator records successful calculations; metadata and failed work do not register. The request accumulator is bounded at 64, with independent policy/Ref per call. HTTP, RPC and both MCP composition paths use this owner; registration omits the first caller's collector. Native waitUntil preserves call context while each send opens its own operation scope. Pure tax/local SDK paths remain separate.
- Relay checks fixed path/US destination, exact origin, method, closed retry query and media types; retains complete bytes and uses failing stream bounds. Denied policy precedes body read/delivery. Status/retry projection and caller-header rebuilding are narrow. Streamed success, size crossing and timeout paths are distinct from F1's unconsumed rejection branch.
- Management inventories complete checked pages and every listed project, rejects incomplete/foreign/ambiguous ownership, bounds reads, serialises writes, and does not automatically repeat an uncertain POST. Provider read/diff/reconcile refuse missing retained history or owner replacement. Ordinary delete and bulk nuke retention are explicit. Live registration caches fallible management acquisition without a package/runtime escape.

## Limits, recovery and return to owner

This review does not choose or implement a browser sender, one-project target, cross-app adoption, credential policy, analytics activation, telemetry/metrics, deployment, provider apply, package publication or merge. After fixes, the primary owner must run relevant focused checks, reconcile documentation/evidence and qualify the exact corrected source. T010's whole-rebuild terminal review remains unfulfilled by this bounded report.
